sentences.text: To judge risk of collision on radar, mark a target’s position several times over a few minutes.
The line through those marks is its relative motion line.
Extend it past the center of the screen, and the closest distance between that line and your boat is the closest point of approach, or C P A.
The time until you reach it is the T C P A.
Many radars can track targets automatically, called MARPA on small boats or ARPA on ships, and compute C P A for you.
Remember Rule seven: radar plotting or equivalent systematic observation is required, and decisions must not be based on scanty radar information, like a single glance at the screen.
